text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.97% today as oil prices held firm and refining conditions tightened. The spread between world oil (trading at $113.96) and U.S. oil ($96.17) widened to nearly $18 per barrel, creating favorable margins for refiners like COP that process crude into diesel and gasoline. Goldman Sachs's warning that diesel prices will remain high through 2027 due to refinery capacity constraints suggests sustained strong margins for oil majors with refining operations.

Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East are also bolstering oil prices and investor appetite for energy stocks. Attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and the ongoing conflict in the Red Sea have kept oil markets on edge, with Brent crude hovering around $100 a barrel despite the recent Yemeni forces' tactical win. These supply risks mean refiners and oil producers may benefit from elevated and volatile pricing for months to come.
